text:
Carmen Liu: Quick sync on a pattern I think we haven't explicitly discussed: a "covenant" between policy authors and runtime about expiry intent vs enforced safety. We're getting mismatch bugs.
Devon Park: Nice term. What's the covenant shape?
Carmen Liu: Policy publishes an `expiry_intent` (nullable) + human-friendly `reason`. Runtime publishes `safety_cap` per deployment (never exceeds this). When mismatch happens, runtime writes a "consensus_clamp" record explaining why.
Rohit Garg: So runtime can shorten but not lengthen intent? That matches previous threads but covenant formalizes the contract and metadata.
Leah Kim: Agree. We should add fields: `intent_source` (cli|console|api), `intent_reason`, `consensus_clamp:{effective_expiry, reason, actor}` recorded as audit.
Devon Park: For private/on-prem, we need signed covenant bundles. Control plane signs and pushes, or local-admin can sign. Runtime validates signature and honors the local `safety_cap`.
Carmen Liu: Also add a lightweight "prune_coordinator" role. If control-plane mode, coordinator is centralized and issues prune batches. If local-only mode, runtime becomes coordinator but must honor signed bundle.
Rohit Garg: Operationally, coordinator should support a two-step prune: 1) mark `soft_deprecate` (emit header), 2) phased drain (traffic percent -> 0), 3) prune. Each step emits telemetry.
Leah Kim: Header idea: `X-Rdwd-Route-State: soft;eta=2026-05-01T12:00:00Z;percent=40` so proxies can see current drain percentage.
PolicyBot: Schema suggestion snippet:
```
route:
  id: "promo-eu-lowcost"
  match: {region: eu-west}
  expiry_intent_seconds: 1209600
  intent_reason: "campaign end"
  metadata: {owner: "@carmen"}
  covenant_signed_by: "control-plane-v1"
```
Devon Park: Telemetry contract: events `covenant.accepted`, `covenant.clamped`, `coordinator.step` with tags: route_id, policy_id, declared, effective, clamp_actor, coordinator_mode. Keep payload small.
Rohit Garg: For automated clamps we should require multi-signal confirmation (e.g., latency spike AND GPU OOMs) before shortening intent automatically. No single noisy metric should trigger a clamp.
Leah Kim: Good. Propose simple consensus rule: need >=2 distinct signal groups (infra, latency, error-rate) with thresholds within a window before auto-clamp. Also provide an escape-hatch for ops to force a clamp with `operator_override` that is timeboxed and audited.
Carmen Liu: Migration: accept both `expiry_intent_seconds` and legacy `ttl` for 8 weeks. Runtime emits a `covenant-warning` when legacy used. Linter warns in CI.
Devon Park: Coordinator placement: default control-plane, fallback local. Add `--coordinator-mode={control,local,dry-run}` for runtime. Dry-run prints planned clamps to logs and telemetry but doesn't enforce.
Rohit Garg: Testing: add `covenant-sim` harness to simulate signals and verify consensus clamps and coordinator steps. Also add unit for signed bundles and key rotation.
Leah Kim: Docs: covenant contract, schema examples, coordinator modes, emergency runbook, CLI commands (`redwood policy sign-bundle`, `redwood route covenant-preview --policy`), and a short FAQ for private customers.
DeployBot: Note: created ticket RW-PLT-7123 "covenant & prune_coordinator" and assigned Carmen+Devon+Rohit.
Carmen Liu: Next steps: I'll draft covenant RFC with data model + telemetry. Devon will prototype coordinator modes. R ohit to design consensus rules. Leah to update linter and docs. Revisit in 72h. :rocket:
